description: openLCA 2.8.2 names metal ions with a Stock numeral or the generic marker -- `Cadmium II`, `Arsenic V`, `Copper Ion` -- and writes the bare metal's registry number on 339 of those rows under 29 names: 7440-43-9 on `Cadmium II`, 7439-92-1 on `Lead II`. The number route runs before the name route, so on the six-list build of 21 October 2026 (commit 931ed30) every one of them reached the metal, while the sibling rows carrying the ion's own number reached the ion: `Cadmium II` was two substances depending on which number came with it, and the lookup read the name three ways (#380). The merge now sets a bare element's number aside where the row's name states an ion (`merge.species.element_number_set_aside`), the row is placed by its name through the ion naming standard, and the mapping's basis reads `label+element-number-set-aside` with the number. The lookup prepares a query the same way. One claim per name, on a row that shipped the metal's number -- the record's own `cas` is empty once the number is set aside, so a selector on the number would find nothing; the two substance claims hold cadmium's numbers apart. Twenty-four rows that carry EF 3.1's own uuids for the elements GreenDelta renamed stay on EF's flows by uuid (#347) and are outside the rule.

expectations.title: openLCA's `Aluminium III` under the metal's number reaches `Aluminium(3+)` with the number set aside
expectations.comment: One of the 10 `Aluminium III` rows that shipped the metal's number; all 10 reach `Aluminium(3+)` with the basis `label+element-number-set-aside` on the six-list build of 21 October 2026 (commit 7a5a1b6), where on the build before it (commit 931ed30) they reached the metal by the number. Of the name's 23 rows, 13 by the ion's own number reach the ion as well.

expectations.title: One substance carries cadmium's number 7440-43-9 and it is called Cadmium
expectations.comment: The rule sets the number aside rather than carrying it onto the ion: a `Cadmium(2+)` under the metal's number would be a second substance on the number, which the number route would then find for every bare `Cadmium` row.

expectations.title: One substance carries cadmium(2+)'s number 22537-48-0 and it is called Cadmium(2+)
expectations.comment: Where openLCA's 38 `Cadmium II` rows meet ecoinvent's 19 and BAFU's one.

expectations.title: openLCA's `Potassium I` taken from the ground reaches `Potassium`, not `Potassium(1+)`
expectations.comment: A metal taken from the ground is the element, whatever its name says about charge. GreenDelta scores this row 1.6e-08 in `Resource use, minerals and metals`, which is exactly what the JRC states for `Potassium` in the ground, and EF 3.1 has no ion among its ground resources. On the six-list build of 22 October 2026 (commit 5a343f5) the #380 rule sent it to `Potassium(1+)` in `Resource → Ground`, a flow only openLCA's rows fed; 35 openLCA rows were placed that way. Ruled by the project owner on 23 October 2026: a resource in the ground is never an ion. Resources in water are not covered, because ecoinvent ships dissolved ions there under the ion's own number.

expectations.comment: Ships 17341-25-2, the sodium ion's number, under the bare name and filed as a resource. On the six-list build of 22 October 2026 (commit 5a343f5) the number route sent it to `Sodium(1+)` in the ground, beside ecoinvent's dissolved `Sodium I` in water: one of the seven substances `0450-no-substance-is-published-in-two-places` counted.

expectations.title: openLCA's `Cadmium II` emitted to agricultural soil under the metal's number still reaches `Cadmium(2+)`
expectations.comment: The other half of the ground-resource rule: only resources in the ground are read as the element. An emission keeps the ion its name states.
